title: Kuril Islands: Moscow and Beijing close ranks against Tokyo
gist: Bernal argues the Kuril Islands dispute is hardening as Russia declares relations with Japan 'reduced to zero' and China tilts toward Moscow's position, while Washington courts both — leaving Tokyo isolated, constrained by Russian LNG dependence (~10% of 2025 imports), and likely to accelerate a regional militarisation spiral that could pull in Seoul.

themes.theme: Russia–Japan relations frozen over the Kurils

insights.claim: Russia suspended peace-treaty negotiations with Japan in March 2022 over Ukraine-related sanctions, and in February 2026 the Kremlin declared relations 'reduced to zero' because of Japan's 'unfriendly stance'.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: No near-term path to Russia–Japan normalisation; Japanese firms' Russia exposure stays at political risk.

insights.claim: Japan has imposed sanctions on Russia more than 20 times since 2022, most recently on 2 October banning services to 35 'shadow fleet' vessels transporting Russian oil.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Tightening shadow-fleet enforcement marginally constrains Russian crude export logistics.

insights.claim: Putin's first visit to the southern Kurils in August 2026 signalled that, from Moscow's perspective, the territorial question is settled.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Territorial dispute effectively closed from Russia's side — expect no concessions.

themes.theme: China tilts toward Moscow on the islands

insights.claim: In July 2026 Chinese and Russian naval vessels conducted joint navigation around Japan and held live-fire exercises inside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Sino-Russian military coordination around Japan elevates Northeast Asian security risk and supports Japan defence spending.

insights.claim: A Chinese delegation visited Iturup (Etorofu) on 13 October to explore joint projects including fisheries, and Beijing invoked 'the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War' — echoing Moscow's justification and reversing Mao Zedong's 1960s support for returning the islands to Japan.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Marks a deliberate Chinese diplomatic shift against Japan; watch for Chinese commercial activity on the Kurils.
insights.quote: the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War must always be respected and upheld

insights.claim: Beijing's recalibration is likely driven by perceived Japanese militarisation and PM Sanae Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan, and China prefers Russian control because islands returned to Japan could one day host US forces.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Japan–China tensions are structural, linked to Taiwan; expect continued Chinese pressure on Japan.
insights.quote: islands returned to Japan could one day host US military personnel or equipment

themes.theme: Japan's constraints: energy, capabilities, US reliability

insights.claim: Under Takaichi, Japan's defence budget has exceeded $58 billion for the first time, and she told parliament Japan would 'deepen concrete and realistic considerations' on sea-lane defence including nuclear-powered submarines.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for Japanese defence contractors (shipbuilding, submarines).

insights.claim: Nuclear-powered submarines remain a difficult prospect for Japan given their technological demands and the Self-Defence Forces' serious personnel shortages.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Temper expectations on speed of Japan's SSN programme.

insights.claim: Japan holds stakes in Sakhalin-2 and roughly 10% of its 2025 LNG imports came from Russia, giving Moscow leverage; Putin has said Russia would support Japanese companies that keep working with it.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Sakhalin-2 is a pressure point; any disruption would tighten Asian LNG and lift JKM prices.
insights.quote: roughly 10% of the liquefied natural gas it imported in 2025 came from Russia

insights.claim: As US–China relations improve and Trump pursues better ties with Putin, a more conciliatory US approach toward Beijing, Moscow and Pyongyang could leave room for further provocations against Japan.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: US détente with rivals raises, not lowers, Japan-specific geopolitical risk.

insights.claim: Diversifying energy supply including through closer cooperation with Europe would reduce Moscow's leverage over Japan but would do little to resolve the islands dispute.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Watch Japanese LNG contracting shifts away from Russia.

insights.claim: Takaichi's electoral mandate, a worsening threat environment and doubts about US reliability are likely to push Tokyo further toward military options despite pacifist constitutional constraints.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal

insights.claim: Japanese militarisation would give Beijing and Moscow greater incentive to deepen military cooperation, and Seoul — facing North Korea and similar US-alliance doubts — may follow Japan, intensifying a vicious cycle.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Regional arms race supports Korean and Japanese defence equities.

insights.claim: Seoul–Tokyo defence cooperation could help both, but historical disagreements limit it, so militarisation is likely to accelerate in the short term.
insights.speaker: Gabriela Bernal
insights.so_what: Defence spending trend in Northeast Asia is up and accelerating.
insights.quote: the trend towards greater militarisation seems likely to accelerate in the short term
